brief: Design an interface for negotiating with a sentient building's mood system, where users must balance the competing desires of different rooms that have developed distinct personalities—the kitchen dem

dominant_strengths: Clean typographic hierarchy with consistent uppercase labels and bold percentages reads with calm Swiss-style restraint
Disciplined whitespace and card rhythm create a legible three-zone layout that is easy to parse
Restrained mono-blue accent against neutral grays keeps minimalism coherent and uncluttered
dominant_weaknesses: Completely ignores the brief: no sentient rooms, no personalities, no kitchen/bedroom/etc. negotiation—just abstract input/output dials
Generic dashboard vocabulary (sliders, percentages, coherence score) carries zero emotional or characterful resonance
Central circle is visually inert—floating dot lacks affordance, motion cues, or any sense of mood/personality
fix_priorities: Replace abstract states with named room agents (Kitchen, Library...) each with distinct mood signatures and demands
Introduce expressive visual language—tension lines, competing color fields, anthropomorphic glyphs—conveying conflict between rooms
Reframe controls as negotiation/dialogue mechanics rather than generic balance/intensity sliders
Animate the central orb to reflect mood drift and disagreement rather than a static blue dot
rationale.norman_balance: Behaviorally legible and visceral-clean, but reflectively empty—the design tells no story about what it is for.
rationale.intent_fit: Fails the brief: this is a generic mediation/coherence dashboard with no trace of sentient rooms or personality negotiation.
